title.en: The People of the Bench (Ahl al-Suffa)

region.zh: 麥地那清真寺廊簷（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877); cf. Sahih al-Bukhari narrations on Ahl al-Suffa

texts.license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: The homeless of the first Muslim community — men of no tribe and no house in Medina — are given the shadowed bench in the mosque, the Suffa. The Prophet sits with them; the wealthier Companions send them their supper; and the tradition counts among them the men who would become the first scholars and the first saints. The bench is the first institution of the poor of Islam.
summary.zh: 首個穆斯林社團中的無家者——無部落、無麥地那居所之人——被安置於清真寺的蔭廊長凳（蘇法）。先知與之同坐；富裕聖門弟子送晚飯；傳統中不乏日後的首批學者與聖徒。此長凳乃伊斯蘭窮人制度之始。

sensitivity.note: Sira/hadith tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: The homeless of the first Muslim community were given the shadowed bench at the back of the mosque of Medina — the Suffa — where they lodged and learned; men of no house in Medina, some of them of no tribe at all. The Prophet sat with them, and the wealthier Companions sent them their supper.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.

passages.text: The tradition counts among the People of the Bench the men who became the first scholars and saints of Islam, and the story is told of one of them who had nothing but his cloak and his patience, and of the Prophet who said: 'Whoever of my people keeps one of these men shall keep his Prophet.' The bench is the first institution of the poor of Islam, and the first school.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.

region.en: Valley of Ranuna, near Quba (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫巴附近拉努納谷（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Sira material from Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767) via Ibn Hisham; English: Muir, Life of Mahomet (1877)

source.work: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (Arabic); English: William Muir, The Life of Mahomet (Smith, Elder, 1877)

texts.license: Public domain (English edition 1877; Arabic original 9th century)

summary.en: On the road from Quba to Medina, on a Friday, the Prophet stops in the valley of Ranuna among the Banu Salim ibn Awf and leads them in the first congregational prayer of the new rite — the prayer of the congregation (jumu'ah), with the sermon. The mosque of Friday becomes the pattern of every mosque of the empire.
summary.zh: 自庫巴至麥地那途中，值周五，先知於拉努納谷薩里姆·本·奧夫部族中，率領首次新儀的集體禮拜——主麻拜，並講道。周五清真寺成為帝國每一座清真寺的範式。

sensitivity.note: Sira tradition of a living religion; paraphrased from public-domain Arabic/English sources.

passages.text: On the road from Quba to Medina, on a Friday, the Prophet stopped in the valley of Ranuna among the Banu Salim ibn Awf, and led them in the first congregational prayer of the new rite — the prayer of the congregation (jumu'ah), with its sermon; and a hundred men were present. It was the first Friday mosque of Islam.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham, Sira (Muir 1877); not verbatim.

title.zh: 雙生姊妹：該隱殺弟之因

region.en: First settlement of Adam's children (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿丹子女的首處聚居地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qisas al-Anbiya tradition (Arabic, c. 8th-11th centuries CE); paraphrase from Arabic

source.work: Qisas al-Anbiya / tafsir legends (al-Tabari, al-Kisa'i); passages paraphrased from Arabic

texts.license: Arabic original public domain; paraphrase original

summary.en: The legend fills the motive of the first murder: Adam's children were born in twin pairs, boy and girl, and the law of the time was that each brother should marry his own twin-sister from another pair — not his own. Abel's twin was the fairer; Cain refused to take his own and demanded his brother's; Adam bade them offer a sacrifice, and the fire from heaven decided. Cain slew, and the first city was built on the first grave.
summary.zh: 傳說補足首宗謀殺之動機：阿丹子女皆為雙生——一男一女；當時之法，各兄弟當娶另一對的雙生姊妹，而非自己的。亞伯的雙生妹貌美；該隱拒娶己妹而求其弟之妹；阿丹命二人獻祭，天火定奪。該隱殺之；首座城築於首個墳墓之上。

sensitivity.note: Qisas legend of a living tradition; the twin-marriage motif parallels origin-of-death and sibling clusters; paraphrased from the Arabic original; motif tagging is interpretive.

passages.text: Adam's children, the legend says, were born in twin pairs, boy and girl together; and the law of that first age was that each brother should marry his twin-sister from another pair, but not his own. Abel's twin was the fairer of the two; and Cain refused to take his own sister and demanded his brother's.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.

passages.text: Adam bade them settle it by an offering: each to bring a sacrifice, and the fire from heaven to take the acceptable one. The fire came down on Abel's lamb and left Cain's sheaf; and Cain said to his brother, 'I will slay thee.' And he slew him — and the legend adds that the first city of the world was built by the line of Cain on the first grave of the world.
passages.note: Paraphrase of al-Tabari, Tarikh (Arabic); not verbatim.

title.en: Muhammad ibn Qasim and the Conquest of Sind
title.zh: 穆罕默德·本·卡西姆與信德征服

region.en: Indus delta, Debal and Daybul (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 印度河三角洲，迪巴勒（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Event 711-713 CE; English: W. Muir, The Caliphate (1891), ch. 37

source.work: William Muir, The Caliphate (1891), ch. 37 (conquest of Sind); from the Arabic Chachnama tradition

texts.license: Public domain (English edition 1891; Arabic-Persian originals medieval)

summary.en: A girl taken by pirates from Sind calls on the caliph from the slave-market of Baghdad — 'I am a daughter of the chiefs of Sind.' Walid sends the young general Muhammad ibn Qasim with six thousand, and the fort of Debal is taken by the stone-thrower that was carried by five hundred men; the pirates' stronghold falls, and the Indus is opened. The young general is recalled, and the tale of his recall is one of the grey anecdotes of the caliphal court.
summary.zh: 一信德女子被海盜擄至巴格達奴市，向哈里發呼救——『我是信德酋長之女。』瓦利德遣青年統帥穆罕默德·本·卡西姆率六千人，以五百人抬運的投石機攻陷迪巴勒要塞；海盜巢穴傾覆，印度河開通。青年統帥被召回；其召回之事成為哈里發宮廷灰色軼事之一。

sensitivity.note: Early Islamic historiography of the eastern conquests; the Ibn Qasim episode opens eight centuries of Muslim presence in the subcontinent; paraphrased from Muir.

passages.text: A girl taken by pirates from the coast of Sind was set in the slave-market of Baghdad, and she called on the caliph in his own hall: 'I am a daughter of the chiefs of Sind; avenge me.' Walid sent the young general Muhammad ibn Qasim with six thousand men, and the fort of Debal, the pirates' stronghold, was taken by the great stone-thrower that was carried by five hundred.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Chachnama tradition via Muir, The Caliphate (1891), ch. 37; not verbatim.

passages.text: The Indus was opened to the Arabs, and the towns of the river came under tribute; and the young general was recalled in the change of caliphs, and the tale of his recall is told among the grey anecdotes of the court. The conquest of Sind opened eight centuries of Muslim presence in the subcontinent.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Chachnama tradition via Muir, The Caliphate (1891); not verbatim.
